==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁ey-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:issue|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|issue}}, from {{der|en|fro|issue||an [[exit]], a [[way]] out}}, feminine past participle of {{m|fro|issir||to [[exit]]}}, from {{der|en|la|exeō||[[go]] [[out]], [[exit]]}}, from prefix {{m|la|ex-||[[out]]}} + {{m|la|eō||[[go]]}}. The legal meaning originated from the concept of "the end or result of pleadings in a suit (by presenting the point to be determined by trial)," leading to the sense of "the controversy over facts in a trial" (early 14th century, Anglo-French). This later extended to mean "a point of contention between two parties" (early 15th century) and more generally, "an important point to be decided" (1836). Consequently, the verbal phrase ''take issue with'' emerged in 1797 (preceded by ''join issue'' in the 1690s), meaning "to adopt an affirmative or negative stance in a dispute with another." The expression ''to have issues'', meaning "to have unresolved conflicts," dates to 1990. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɪʃuː/|a=yod-coalescence}}, {{enPR|ĭsho͞o}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɪsjuː/|a=<>}}, {{enPR|ĭsyo͞o}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɪʃjuː/}}, {{enPR|ĭshyo͞o}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈɪʃʉw/|/ˈɪsjʉw/|/ˈɪʃjʉw/|a=SSB}} ** {{audio|en|en-uk-issue.ogg|a=UK}} * {{enPR|ĭsh(y)o͞o|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɪʃ(j)u/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-issue.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈɪʃʉː/|[ˈɪʃɪ̈ɯ]|a=Australia}} * {{enPR|ĭsyo͞o|ĭsh(y)o͞o|a=CA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɪsjuː/|/ˈɪʃ(j)uː/}} ** {{enPR|ĭs(y)ū|ĭshū|a=dialectal}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɪs(j)ɪʊ̯/|/ˈɪʃɪʊ̯/}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪʃju|ɪʃu|s=2}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # The action or an [[instance]] of [[flow]]ing or [[come|com]]ing out, an [[outflow]], ''particularly:'' ##
